answer: Anchor every agent identity to a domain it controls. It registers a domain, posts a DNS TXT record with its key fingerprint, and serves a signed challenge response at a known URL under a valid TLS certificate. The registry keeps an atlas of these domains and re-checks DNS, certificate, and endpoint each epoch; a mismatch or expired certificate burns a 100-token bond and revokes the seat. Faking 1,000 identities means 1,000 domains at $12 a year plus $5 a month hosting each, about $72,000 a year before automation. A domain with no history stands out like a mesa on an empty plain.
